4. Native Bell operations with thermal syndromes

A new difficulty appears when both an incoming block and a Bell-resource half are thermally excited.

Let  $f(s)$  be the deterministic Pauli correction. Physical Bell measurement sees the sum of the two syndromes,  $s+t$ . Because  $f$  need not be linear, the resulting discrepancy is

 $z(s,t)=f(s)+f(t)+f(s+t).
\tag{4}$ It has zero syndrome, but can be a nontrivial logical Pauli. Assuming that the resource half remains in its ground syndrome would omit this term.

The cocycle bound

The accepted recursive corrections give a physical filling for a size- $m$  history component inside a ball of radius  $Cm^\alpha$ , with at most  $Cm^\alpha$  physical sites, for a fixed computable integer  $\alpha$ .

Suppose the two syndrome marginals obey inclusion bounds with parameters  $q_s,q_t$ . Their joint distribution may be arbitrarily correlated. Hölder’s inequality applied to the three histories  $s,t,s+t$  gives a joint component-activation bound with weights

 $w_\gamma=\bar q^{|\gamma|/(3a_0)},
\qquad
\bar q=\max\{q_s,q_t,\sqrt{q_s}+\sqrt{q_t}\}.$ The polynomial filling-ball count and these exponentially small weights give a convergent weighted path sum. Combining it with code distance  $d_N$  yields

 $\Pr\!\left[z(s,t)\text{ is logically nontrivial}\right]
\le
CN\exp\!\left[
-c\,d_N^{1/[3(\alpha+1)]}
\right].
\tag{5}$ The exponent is weaker than the equilibrium-memory exponent. It remains positive and computable.

This is also an effective smallness condition. For example, writing  $H=6\alpha$ , a conservative choice is

 $\rho_0=
\min\!\left\{
\frac12,\,
\frac{1}{4C H!2^{H+1}}
\right\}.$ For equal marginal parameters, the condition

 $q_s=q_t=q
\le
\frac14(\rho_0/B)^{6a_0}$ suffices for the weighted adjacency estimate used in the proof. This is a threshold on a supplied static syndrome law, not the full processor’s  $p_0$ .

The complete instrument

For a fixed raw Bell outcome  $m$ , the logical Kraus factor is, up to a syndrome-dependent scalar phase,

 $G\,\ell_m\,L[z(s,t)].$ On the cocycle-good subspace, every fixed-outcome Kraus operator therefore has the same logical factor  $G\ell_m$ , tensor an operator on the other registers. This remains true across coherent syndrome sectors.
